 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.09.2023 at about 04.20 p.m., when he was going in Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-EW-7398, along with his wife and daughter, opposite Varin School Road, Tumkur-Kunigal SH-33, Guluru-Village, Tumkur Taluk & District, a Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22- F-3285, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to him.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Unnathi Multispeciality Hospital, Tumkur, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .4,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant, conveyance and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was Agriculturist and was doing Coolie work and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents have also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondents have contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further 1st respondent has contended that the skoda car was insured with the 2nd respondent vide Policy No.76260131230100008624, valid from 27.08.2023 to 26.08.2024 and the policy was in force at the time of alleged accident.
Further the driver of vehicle was having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. Respondent No.2, in the written statement, has contended that the person who was driving the vehicle in question had no valid and effective driving license to drive Skoda car.

Further this respondent has issued policy No.76260131230100008624 for the period from 27.08.2023 to 26.08.2024 in favour of first respondent and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

sentences.text: Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced first information statement which is marked as Ex.P.2.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, the brother of petitioner by name Sri.Gangaraju S/o Guruvaiah has lodged a complaint with police on 16.09.2023 pertaining to the accident occurred on 15.09.2023.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot Mahazar & sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.3 & 4.
The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that the actual facts at the place accident differ from facts as mentioned in sketch and mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages being caused to the offending car.
The driver or owner of offending car not explained the manner in which the vehicle got damaged.
The said document indicates the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P6 is the notice issued under Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given to said notice is marked as Ex.P.7.
In the notice given by I.O, there is clear mention about involvement of offending vehicle and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Respondent No.1, owner of the car, has given reply to the notice as per Ex.P.7.
In the reply given by respondent No.1, there appears to be no denial about involvement of the vehicle in the accident and also negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the car, is having opportunity to explain the manner of accident as well as damages caused to the vehicle vide reply notice.
But, respondent No.1 neither denied involvement of car in the accident nor denied negligence on the part of driver of the car in the cause of accident.
The said document also discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.8 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
In the petition as well as evidence, petitioner stated about car colliding to the motorcycle from front side.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of collision between the vehicles from behind.
In the first information statement, it is stated that the driver of offending vehicle negligently stopped the vehicle due to which the accident is stated to have occurred.
The respondent No.1 not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said contention.
Though the manner of accident is mentioned wrongly in the petition, same cannot be considered sufficient to doubt or dispute the cause of accident.
The wrong mentioning of manner of accident in the petition will not appear sufficient to consider that the accident has not taken place.
The police records furnished by petitioner clearly indicate the aspect of occurring of accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials to disprove or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to cause of accident.
The manner of accident is stated in the documents furnished by petitioner which has not been rebutted with cogent and substantive materials.

In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to doubt the occurrence of accident, the wrong mentioning of manner of accident cannot be considered sufficient to doubt or dispute the occurrence of accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the Gangaiah vs Parfina Babin .P

The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it can be duly construed that negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.8, wherein it discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced Ex.P9 - Discharge Summary issued by Unnathi Multispeciality Hospital and petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N., as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P16 & 17.
The said document discloses the aspect of treatment availed by the petitioner for the injuries sustained.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability, to the right lower limb at 69% and to the whole body at 23%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.

(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at Hospital.
The petitioner has produced Inpatient Bill for a sum of .2,59,400/- marked at Ex.P.11 and two advance receipts marked at Ex.P.12.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent and substantive evidence.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .2,59,400/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 15.09.2023 and the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of materials, it discloses that the petitioner has admitted to the hospital as an inpatient for treatment of the injuries sustained.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 - Discharge Summary, which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 15.09.2023 to 22.09.2023 i.e., for a period of 08 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 08 days to a sum of .4,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Honnudike Hand Post, Guluru-Hobli, Naruganahalli,
Chikkanayakan Halli Taluk, Tumkur Taluk and District and he has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses towards travelling during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner has contended that he was an Agriculturist and doing Coolie work and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .20,000/- per month.
No materials are placed by petitioner to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:

The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N, working as an Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center examined as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained injuries like right floating knee injury with right femur and right tibia fracture and underwent CRIF with retrograde nailing for the right femur & CRIF with IMIL Nail for the right tibia and later discharged.
Further PW.2 deposed in his evidence that petitioner complained of unable to fold the right knee, unable to sit down, squat and sit cross leg and carry any work as before.
Further on examination, the petitioner has fixed knee with no movements in the right knee.
Further as per X-ray of right leg & right femur shows united fracture with implant in situ and narrowing of right knee joint space.
The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the permanent physical disability for right lower limb at 69% and to the whole body at 23%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.16 & 17 i.e., clinical note and X-ray films.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
PW.2 stated in the cross examination that the fractures are united and the disability of petitioner varies after future surgery.
PW.2 not stated that due to accidental injuries, the petitioner will not be able to do routine work.

The doctor stated that the percentage of disability may vary after future surgery and as per the evidence of doctor, there appears possibility of further improvement in the condition of petitioner after the surgery.
Further the petitioner also examined MRO of Unnathi Multispeciality Hospital as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.18 to 20 i.e., authorization letter, inpatient record and X-ray films.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 12%.

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver.
There appears to be no dispute pertaining to the ownership of respondent No.1 over the vehicle and about issue of policy pertaining to the vehicle by respondent No.2.
The materials on record disclose that the policy of insurance was valid and effective and the driver of offending vehicle was having valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
So, the respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .7,52,040/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Forty only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

The wrong mentioning of manner of accident in the petition will not appear sufficient to consider that the accident has not taken place.
The police records furnished by petitioner clearly indicate the aspect of occurring of accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The respondents not placed satisfactory materials to disprove or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to cause of accident.
The manner of accident is stated in the documents furnished by petitioner which has not been rebutted with cogent and substantive materials.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to doubt the occurrence of accident, the wrong mentioning of manner of accident cannot be considered sufficient to doubt or dispute the occurrence of accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the Gangaiah vs Parfina Babin .P
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it can be duly construed that negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle is the cause for the accident.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Skoda Car bearing Regn.No.KL-22-F-3285 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
No materials are placed by petitioner to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 31 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
